source: Quiz 4 - Sessions 1-5: Building and Improving Agent Skills
question: Why can an agent work with a large project without reading every file into its current context?

options.text: Accessible files are already fully represented in every model input.
options.feedback: Access means material can be retrieved, not that its contents have already been loaded. The current input may contain only a small selection.

options.text: It can search for and read material relevant to the current step.
options.feedback: Useful organization and file tools support selective retrieval. This keeps the current context focused while retaining access to other sources.

options.text: Filenames contain enough detail to replace the original source evidence.
options.feedback: Names help locate material but do not prove its contents. The agent still needs to open the relevant sources.

options.text: A long conversation automatically copies every project file into memory.
options.feedback: Conversation history and available files are different sources of information. File contents need to be retrieved through available tools.
